related_questions.question: When is the best time to test for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: If you have symptoms, test immediately, and then test again per the instructions if your first result is negative. If you were exposed to someone who has COVID-19 and you do not have symptoms, wait at least 5 full days after your exposure before testing. If you test too early, you may have an inaccurate result.

related_questions.question: How soon after getting symptoms should you take a COVID test?
related_questions.snippet: If you have symptoms of COVID-19, test immediately. Keep in mind that a positive result on an antigen test is reliable, but a negative test is not always accurate. If you have symptoms and your antigen test is negative, take another antigen test after 48 hours.

related_questions.question: What symptoms mean I should get a COVID test?
related_questions.snippet: When should I get a COVID-19 test? It's still a good idea to isolate and get a COVID-19 test if you have any cold symptoms, even if they're mild and even if you're fully vaccinated. Symptoms may include sniffles, congestion or a cough. COVID might resemble a mild cold, especially in fully vaccinated people.

related_questions.question: What does the very beginning of COVID feel like?

text_blocks.snippet: The initial symptoms of COVID-19 can feel similar to a mild cold or other respiratory illnesses, with possible symptoms like fatigue, sore throat, and mild cough. Some individuals might also experience a headache or fever. The severity of symptoms can vary widely, and it's important to be mindful of even mild symptoms as they can potentially worsen.
snippet_highlighted_words: similar to a mild cold or other respiratory illnesses, with possible symptoms like fatigue, sore throat, and mild cough

text_blocks.snippet: Early Symptoms (may include, but not limited to):

list.snippet: Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or drained.
Sore Throat: A scratchy or painful throat.
Mild Cough: A cough that may not be severe initially.
Headache: A mild to moderate headache.

list.title: Varied Severity:
list.snippet: Symptoms can range from mild to severe, and some people may not experience any symptoms at all.

list.title: Evolving Symptoms:
list.snippet: Symptoms may start mild and then progress to more severe ones.

list.title: Individual Differences:
list.snippet: Symptoms can vary depending on vaccination status, previous infection, and the specific variant of the virus.

list.title: Consult a Doctor:
list.snippet: If you have concerns about your symptoms, it's always best to consult with a healthcare professional.

text_blocks.snippet: You should consider getting tested for COVID-19 if you have symptoms, have been exposed to someone with COVID-19, or are in a high-risk setting. Testing immediately when symptomatic and again after exposure, if initially negative, is recommended to reduce the spread.
snippet_highlighted_words: if you have symptoms, have been exposed to someone with COVID-19, or are in a high-risk setting

text_blocks.snippet: When to test if you have symptoms:

list.title: Test immediately
list.snippet: if you have any symptoms of COVID-19, such as fever, cough, fatigue, or loss of taste or smell.

list.title: If the initial test is negative,
list.snippet: follow the instructions for repeat testing, as antigen tests may require multiple tests to rule out infection.
Wait at least 5 full days: after exposure before testing if you don't have symptoms.
Testing too early: can result in a false negative.

text_blocks.snippet: Other situations when testing may be recommended:

list.title: High-risk settings:
list.snippet: Consider testing if you are in an area with a medium or high COVID-19 Hospital Admission Level or if you are in contact with people who are at high risk for severe COVID-19 (e.g., older adults or immunocompromised individuals).

list.title: Screening programs:
list.snippet: Some individuals, like healthcare workers or those in congregate living settings, may be required to test regularly as part of a screening program.
